# Chandan Kumar Thakur (The WH2)

Nepal-based AI architect, web developer, and cybersecurity student at Herald College Kathmandu (University of Wolverhampton).

## About
Chandan Kumar Thakur, known as The WH2, develops real-world systems like AI-driven traffic solutions, custom AI platforms such as TalkGPT, and multiple web applications aimed at solving practical problems. He is an ISO certified Frontend Web Developer, a BSc (Hons) Cybersecurity student, and currently works in Research & Development (R&D) at NavaNexa Pvt. Ltd. (Kupondole, Kathmandu) on the N-Traffic Jam project. His portfolio features a highly advanced Terminal Easter Egg (WH2 Shell) containing an arcade-style Snake Game (with 4 difficulties and local leaderboards), Matrix overlays, and system simulation commands. With a strong White Hat mindset, he prioritizes security, deployment, and impact—turning ideas into live, scalable platforms that serve both innovation and national growth.

### Specialized Tools & Utilities
- **The WH2 Knowledge Hub & Workshops:** https://www.chandankumarthakur.com.np/knowledge/ - Real-world technical documentation logs and cybersecurity workshops.
- **BugXploit Ethical Hacking Workshop (2 Weeks):** https://www.chandankumarthakur.com.np/knowledge/ethical-hacking-and-penetration-testing/ - Daily reports and lab configurations from BugXploit (Koteshwor, Kathmandu), instructed by Birendra Sah (https://www.linkedin.com/in/birendrasah4u2/) and Bishal Shrestha (https://www.linkedin.com/in/bishal0x01/). Includes Day 1 (Lab Setup & Foundations), Day 2 (Service Enumeration, VSFTPD 2.3.4 Backdoor Exploitation [CVE-2011-2523] & Metasploit SSH Brute-Force), Day 3 (Active vs Passive Reconnaissance, Bugcrowd Tesla Scope, Google Dorking, DNSDumpster, crt.sh, WHOIS, MXToolbox, Emkei Spoofing Analysis, Wayback Machine API Hunting, and Shodan IoT Intelligence), Day 4 (OS Command Injection on DVWA, PHP shell execution, security tiers in security.php, Burp Suite HTTP proxy interception, HTTP method conversion from GET to POST, anti-CSRF token bypass mechanisms, and weaponized CSRF PoC generation using csrfshark.github.io), Day 5 (Burp Suite Intruder Sniper brute-force attack on DVWA, automated database takeover via SQLMap in Kali Linux [--dbs, -D dvwa --tables, -T users --dump], HTML injection with <b> tags, Reflected XSS [<script>alert(1)</script>], Stored XSS with client-side maxlength bypass via DevTools, iFrame injection, and session cookie hijacking exfiltration via Webhook.site), and Day 6 (ProjectDiscovery Nuclei automated vulnerability scanning against DVWA on Metasploitable 2 with authenticated cookie injection, 69 findings terminal triage [CVE-2012-1823 PHP-CGI query execution, Samba 3.0.20 CVE-2026-4480, DistCC daemon CVE-2004-2687, default PostgreSQL blank passwords, VNC RFB logins, vsftpd 2.3.4 manual terminal verification, missing HTTP security headers], GitHub reconnaissance dorks [org:target api_key], deep dive into streaak/keyhacks for safe API key validation [AWS STS, Stripe, Twilio, Google Maps, Slack], iscan.today, Benji Trapp dork list, and TruffleHog git entropy scanning).
- **WH2 Knowledge Hub (External App):** https://wh2hub.netlify.app/ - Platform for project hosting and knowledge sharing.
